keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «많은 언어가 사라질 위험에 놓여 있다(문제)» 와 «사라져 가는 언어를 지키는 것은 인류의 지식과 문화 다양성을 지키는 일(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the problem (many languages are in danger of disappearing) and the conclusion (protecting them protects human knowledge and cultural diversity). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why might young people feel cut off from their own history?
qs.qko: 왜 젊은이들은 자신의 역사와 단절된 느낌을 받을 수 있을까요?
opts: because they have lost their ancestors' language
because they have moved to big cities
because scientists study their local plants
evs: Some have only a few elderly speakers left, and children are no longer learning them.
When young people lose their ancestors' language, they may feel cut off from their own history.
This knowledge can be valuable to scientists studying medicine or the environment.
Hawaiian, for instance, was once spoken by very few children, but immersion schools have helped bring it back into daily life.
why: 조상의 언어를 잃으면 자기 역사와 끊어진 느낌을 받을 수 있다고 했어요.
The text says that when young people lose their ancestors' language, they may feel cut off from their history.

qs.q: In the sentence about Hawaiian, what does "bring it back into daily life" mean?
qs.qko: 하와이어 문장에서 «bring it back into daily life» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: make people use the language again every day
take the language to another country
keep the language only in old books
evs: When a language disappears, what exactly is lost?
Fortunately, some communities are working to revive their languages through schools, recordings, and apps.
Languages also carry stories, songs, and traditions that give a community its identity.
Each language contains a unique way of understanding the world, built up over many generations.
why: 바로 앞 문장에서 공동체들이 언어를 «되살리려고(revive)» 노력한다고 했어요. 하와이어는 그 예로, 다시 일상에서 쓰이게 된 거예요.
The sentence before says communities are working to revive their languages. Hawaiian is an example: people use it in daily life again.

qs.q: Why can losing a language also be a loss for science?
qs.qko: 왜 언어를 잃는 것이 과학에도 손실이 될 수 있을까요?
opts: Indigenous languages hold detailed knowledge of plants, animals, and weather.
Scientists can only speak indigenous languages.
evs: For example, many indigenous languages have detailed words for local plants, animals, and weather patterns.
Some have only a few elderly speakers left, and children are no longer learning them.
This knowledge can be valuable to scientists studying medicine or the environment.
Fortunately, some communities are working to revive their languages through schools, recordings, and apps.
why: 원주민 언어에는 지역 식물, 동물, 날씨에 대한 자세한 낱말이 있고, 이 지식은 의학이나 환경을 연구하는 과학자에게 소중해요.
Indigenous languages have detailed words for local plants, animals, and weather, and this knowledge is valuable to scientists.

ends: Find out how immersion schools helped bring Hawaiian back.
몰입 학교가 하와이어를 어떻게 되살렸는지 알아봐요.
Learn about words in other languages that have no English match.
영어로 딱 맞는 말이 없는 다른 언어의 낱말을 알아봐요.

write.src: “It is important to <u>learn our grandparents’ stories</u> because <u>they show where we come from</u>.”

write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write an important action and your reason in English.

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «because» 뒤에 «누가/무엇이 + 어떻게 한다» 를 넣어 이유를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: because songs carry our history)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «because», write who or what + what it does to make your reason clear. (e.g. because songs carry our history)
